note: Product- and bundle-specific applicability assessment. NOT_APPLICABLE always carries a cited legal rationale; CONDITIONALLY_APPLICABLE always carries the condition that would change applicability. A product definition is not a tested product; applicability of an instrument is not conformity with it. No CE marking, wheelmark, NMEA certification or marine approval is claimed.

instruments.name: Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU (including delegated cybersecurity acts)
Consumer and commercial law (CRD, CSD, DCD, UCPD, Price Indication, TRLGDCU, LSSI, LCD, LGP)
Radio spectrum and maritime radio rules (Ley 11/2022, ITU-R M.1371, AIS receive-only scope)

productFamilies.productType: Navigation software and licensed-data application, optionally bundled with hardware

assessments.rationale: Standalone NAV software is not apparatus placed on the market; an EMC assessment becomes necessary if NAV ships pre-installed on a HUB, DISPLAY or appliance supplied by EMBARCARTE.
assessments.condition: NAV is supplied on or with electrical hardware placed on the market.
evidenceRequired: System EMC test for the supplied configuration

assessments.rationale: NAV, as defined, performs no intentional radio transmission or reception; radio functions belong to HUB/AIS/WATCH hardware. If NAV is embedded in radio equipment, the RED applies to that equipment instead.
NAV is software/data and has no electrical equipment within the 50-1000 V AC / 75-1500 V DC scope; any bundled appliance is assessed as its own product.
Software alone is not a GPSR product, but the general safety framework applies to any physical product supplied with NAV; the bundle is assessed as hardware.
assessments.condition: NAV is sold with or pre-installed on a physical product.
evidenceRequired: Product safety assessment for the supplied configuration

assessments.rationale: NAV is a product with digital elements made available on the market, including subscription and cloud-connected editions; CRA essential requirements, vulnerability handling, support period and reporting apply.
NAV software contains no electrical or electronic equipment unless it is supplied on hardware, in which case RoHS applies to that hardware.
WEEE applies to electrical and electronic equipment; pure software is out of scope, and any bundled hardware is registered separately.
NAV software contains no batteries; battery obligations attach to the hardware families that contain them.
NAV software is not a recreational craft or a component listed in the RCD scope; the RCD applies to the craft or covered components, not to navigation software.
NAV is not shipborne marine equipment listed for MED wheelmark; no wheelmark claim is made.
The revised PLD covers software and digital products, so NAV and its update stream can fall within the liability regime even without physical hardware.
Consumer sales, subscriptions and claims are subject to CRD/CSD/DCD/UCPD, the Price Indication Directive and Spanish consumer and advertising law; B2B terms require a separate contract set.
NAV does not transmit or receive radio signals directly; AIS reception and radio conformity belong to the AIS/HUB hardware family.
NAV processes account data, track history and location data, so GDPR/LOPDGDD transparency, lawful basis, retention and rights apply.

productFamilies.productType: Networked marine data hub and appliance

assessments.rationale: HUB is apparatus placed on the market with active electronics and networking; it must not cause or suffer electromagnetic disturbance beyond the essential requirements. If HUB is radio equipment, the RED carries the EMC requirement instead.
HUB may include Wi-Fi/Bluetooth or cellular modules; intentional radio transmitters or receivers bring the product within the RED, which then carries the EMC requirement.
assessments.condition: A radio module or antenna is integrated into the shipped HUB.

assessments.rationale: HUB is normally 12/24 V DC and outside the LVD voltage scope; a mains-powered variant within 50-1000 V AC would bring the LVD into scope.
assessments.condition: A mains-voltage variant is placed on the market.
evidenceRequired: Electrical safety test if in scope

assessments.rationale: HUB is a consumer product placed on the market; safety, traceability, warnings and incident duties apply.
HUB is a connected product with digital elements; CRA essential requirements, vulnerability handling, update support and incident reporting apply from the relevant dates.
HUB is electrical and electronic equipment; restricted-substance compliance and DoC are required.
HUB is EEE placed on the Spanish market; producer registration, take-back, marking and reporting apply.
HUB may include a backup battery or be supplied with one; the Batteries Regulation applies to any battery placed on the market with the product.
assessments.condition: A battery is included in the shipped product or packaging.

assessments.rationale: HUB is an electronics product, not a recreational craft or a listed RCD component; the craft's own RCD conformity is the builder's responsibility.
HUB is not shipborne marine equipment placed on an EU ship and no wheelmark claim is made.
HUB is a product and its software can be defective; PLD liability covers hardware, firmware and connected-product updates.
Consumer sales of HUB are subject to CRD/CSD, the Spanish 3-year guarantee and fair-claims rules; B2B sales require separate terms.
Radio transmission by an integrated Wi-Fi/cellular module requires authorised spectrum use and radio conformity; receive-only operation remains subject to radio-equipment rules.
assessments.condition: The shipped HUB transmits radio signals.

assessments.rationale: HUB processes device identifiers, telemetry and potentially location data; GDPR/LOPDGDD transparency and security apply.

productFamilies.productType: Receive-only AIS receiver and connected edition

assessments.rationale: AIS is radio equipment: the RED carries the EMC essential requirement, and the EMC Directive expressly does not additionally apply to radio equipment covered by the RED.
The receiver intentionally receives radio waves (AIS VHF), so it is radio equipment under the RED; safety, EMC and spectrum requirements plus conformity assessment apply.
AIS receiver hardware is typically 12/24 V DC and outside the LVD scope; a mains-powered variant or a power supply within the voltage limits would bring it into scope.
assessments.condition: A mains-voltage variant or supplied power supply is placed on the market.

assessments.rationale: AIS is a consumer product placed on the market; safety, traceability, warnings and incident duties apply, including antenna installation warnings.
AIS-CONNECTED is a product with digital elements and is in scope; a purely local receiver without network capability may be outside the CRA's connected-product scope, which must be confirmed.
assessments.condition: The edition includes network connectivity or software updates.

assessments.rationale: AIS is electrical and electronic equipment subject to RoHS.
AIS is EEE placed on the Spanish market; producer responsibility applies.
AIS receiver hardware is defined without a battery; if a backup battery is added, the Batteries Regulation would apply to it.
AIS is not a recreational craft or an RCD-listed component.
AIS is not shipborne MED equipment and no wheelmark is claimed; a receiver for leisure craft does not become MED equipment by being installed on a yacht.
A defective receiver or misleading reception expectations can cause reliance loss; the PLD applies.
AIS consumer sales are subject to consumer terms, guarantee and fair-claims rules, including the prohibition on transponder/collision-avoidance claims.

AIS reception uses maritime radio frequencies; the receiver must be authorised/conformant and no transmission may be offered. Transmission would require a maritime radio authorisation MAREA does not hold.
A local receiver may process no personal data; AIS-CONNECTED or fleet-shared data can identify vessels and owners, bringing GDPR into scope.
assessments.condition: AIS data is transmitted to EMBARCARTE or shared with other users.

productFamilies.productType: Supervised steering controller and drive interface (safety gate BLOCKED)

assessments.rationale: PILOT includes active electronics and motor drive interfaces; if the product is radio equipment the RED carries the EMC requirement, otherwise the EMC Directive applies.
assessments.condition: The shipped controller is not radio equipment.

assessments.rationale: A remote control or wireless link would make PILOT radio equipment; a wired-only controller is not.
assessments.condition: A wireless control or telemetry radio is integrated.

assessments.rationale: PILOT is normally 12/24 V DC; a mains-powered variant would fall within the LVD scope.
assessments.condition: A mains-powered variant is placed on the market.

assessments.rationale: PILOT is a consumer product with safety implications; GPSR safety, traceability and incident duties apply, and the safety gate must keep it off the market.
PILOT is a connected product with digital elements; CRA security, update and reporting duties apply alongside the safety gate.
PILOT is electrical equipment subject to RoHS.
PILOT is EEE placed on the Spanish market, if it were ever placed, and producer responsibility would apply.
A backup battery in the controller would bring the Batteries Regulation into scope.
assessments.condition: A battery is included in the product.

assessments.rationale: Whether a steering controller is a 'component' under the RCD or an add-on outside its scope has not been determined; the answer changes the conformity route and cannot be assumed.
assessments.condition: A product-scope legal analysis determines whether PILOT is RCD-covered.

assessments.rationale: PILOT is not shipborne MED equipment and no wheelmark claim is made.
A steering product is a high-risk product; the PLD applies to hardware and software, and the safety gate must remain closed until the liability assessment is complete.
Any consumer offer would be subject to consumer and fair-claims law; PILOT must not be offered while the safety gate is BLOCKED.
Any wireless link would require radio conformity and authorised spectrum use; a wired-only installation is not radio equipment.
assessments.condition: A wireless remote or telemetry link is shipped.

assessments.rationale: PILOT may process vessel position and control data; if linked to an account or cloud, GDPR applies.
assessments.condition: Control/telemetry data is linked to an identified user or vessel owner.

assessments.rationale: SENSE modules are active electronic apparatus placed on the market; EMC essential requirements apply unless a module is radio equipment covered by the RED.
Wireless sensor variants (for example wireless wind or tank sensors) are radio equipment; wired variants are not.
assessments.condition: The module intentionally transmits or receives radio waves.

assessments.rationale: SENSE modules are normally 12/24 V DC and outside the LVD scope; a mains-powered variant would be in scope.
assessments.condition: A mains-powered variant is placed on the market.

assessments.rationale: SENSE is a consumer product placed on the market; safety, installation warnings and traceability apply.
Network-connected SENSE modules shipped with firmware fall in scope; a dumb analogue sensor without digital elements may not.
assessments.condition: The module ships firmware or network connectivity.

assessments.rationale: SENSE is electrical and electronic equipment subject to RoHS.
SENSE is EEE placed on the Spanish market; producer responsibility applies.
Battery-powered sensor variants bring the Batteries Regulation into scope; wired variants do not contain batteries.
assessments.condition: A battery is integrated or supplied.

assessments.rationale: SENSE modules are not recreational craft or RCD-listed components.
SENSE is not shipborne MED equipment and no wheelmark is claimed.
Incorrect sensor measurements can cause reliance loss; the PLD applies to the hardware and firmware.
SENSE consumer sales are subject to consumer terms, guarantee and accurate measurement claims.
Wireless sensors require radio conformity and authorised spectrum use.
assessments.condition: The module uses a radio link.

assessments.rationale: A local sensor may process no personal data; cloud-synced sensor data linked to a vessel or owner falls within GDPR.
assessments.condition: Measurements are linked to an identified user or vessel.

productFamilies.productType: Connected remote monitoring device and alert service

assessments.rationale: WATCH includes cellular radio equipment; the RED carries the EMC essential requirement and the EMC Directive does not additionally apply to radio equipment covered by the RED.
WATCH intentionally transmits over cellular networks and is radio equipment; RED essential requirements and conformity assessment apply.
WATCH is battery-powered and normally outside the LVD scope; a supplied mains charger within the voltage limits would bring the charger into scope.
assessments.condition: A mains charger or power supply is supplied with the product.

assessments.rationale: WATCH is a consumer product with safety and monitoring implications; GPSR safety, traceability and incident duties apply.
WATCH is a connected product with digital elements and a cloud service; CRA essential requirements, vulnerability handling, support period and reporting apply.
WATCH is EEE subject to RoHS.
WATCH is EEE placed on the Spanish market; producer responsibility applies.
WATCH contains a battery placed on the market with the product; the Batteries Regulation applies.
WATCH is not a recreational craft or RCD-listed component.
WATCH is not shipborne MED equipment and no wheelmark is claimed.
Missed or delayed alerts and device defects can cause reliance loss; the PLD applies to the device and service.
WATCH hardware and subscription sales are subject to consumer terms, the 3-year guarantee and fair-claims rules; no guaranteed alert claim is allowed.
Cellular transmission uses licensed spectrum through an operator; the device must be radio-conformant and the connectivity contract must exist.
WATCH processes location, vessel identity, account data and alert recipients; a DPIA is likely required.
DISPLAY is active electronic apparatus; EMC essential requirements apply unless it is radio equipment covered by the RED.
A DISPLAY with Wi-Fi/Bluetooth or cellular connectivity is radio equipment; a wired-only display is not.
assessments.condition: A radio module is integrated into the shipped DISPLAY.

assessments.rationale: DISPLAY is normally 12/24 V DC and outside the LVD scope; a mains-powered variant or supplied power supply within the voltage limits is in scope.
assessments.condition: A mains-voltage variant or power supply is placed on the market.

assessments.rationale: DISPLAY is a consumer product placed on the market; safety, traceability and installation warnings apply.
DISPLAY ships firmware and network capability; CRA essential requirements and lifecycle duties apply.
DISPLAY is EEE subject to RoHS.
DISPLAY is EEE placed on the Spanish market; producer responsibility applies.
A backup battery inside DISPLAY would bring the Batteries Regulation into scope.
assessments.condition: A battery is integrated into the display.

assessments.rationale: Whether a display installed as a fixed navigation instrument is an RCD-covered component has not been determined; a scope analysis is required before any conformity route is chosen.
assessments.condition: A product-scope legal analysis determines RCD coverage.

assessments.rationale: DISPLAY is not shipborne MED equipment and no wheelmark is claimed.
A defective display or runtime can mislead navigation; the PLD applies.
DISPLAY consumer sales are subject to consumer terms and fair-claims rules.
Wireless display variants require radio conformity and authorised spectrum use.
assessments.condition: The display uses a radio link.

assessments.rationale: A local display may process no personal data; cloud-linked chart/track data can be personal data.
assessments.condition: Display data is synced to an account or cloud service.

productFamilies.productType: Weather forecast subscription service with licensed data

assessments.rationale: WEATHER is a data service, not electrical apparatus placed on the market; any hardware that displays it is assessed as its own product.
WEATHER performs no radio transmission or reception; connectivity belongs to the user's device or the WATCH/HUB hardware.
WEATHER is a service with no electrical equipment within the LVD scope.
The GPSR applies to products, not to a forecast data service; if WEATHER is sold with a physical device, that device is assessed separately.

A remote data service alone is generally outside the CRA's 'product with digital elements' scope, but the CRA may apply where the service is integral to a product or the client software is placed on the market.
assessments.condition: The CRA consolidated scope analysis concludes that the service or app is in scope.

assessments.rationale: WEATHER software/data has no electrical equipment; RoHS applies to the hardware that displays it.
WEEE applies to EEE, not to a subscription service; the hardware is registered separately.
The WEATHER offering is a software or data service and contains no battery placed on the market; the Batteries Regulation applies to battery-containing hardware, not to the service itself.
WEATHER is not a recreational craft or RCD component.
WEATHER is not shipborne MED equipment and no wheelmark is claimed.
The revised PLD covers software and digital services; forecast errors presented as reliable can ground liability.
Weather subscriptions are digital services subject to DCD, CRD and fair-claims rules, including probabilistic-forecast disclosures.
WEATHER does not transmit or receive radio signals itself.
WEATHER processes account data and possibly location preferences, so GDPR transparency and lawful basis apply.
FLEET is a hosted B2B service; any hardware used with it is a separate product assessed in its own family.
FLEET performs no radio transmission or reception itself.
FLEET is a software service with no electrical equipment.
FLEET is not a product placed on the market; GPSR does not apply to a pure SaaS offering.

The CRA addresses products with digital elements; a pure SaaS service is generally outside its scope, but integrated clients or remote-processing features that are part of a product can bring obligations.
assessments.condition: The CRA scope analysis concludes FLEET or its client software is in scope.

assessments.rationale: FLEET is software and contains no EEE subject to RoHS.
FLEET is not EEE placed on the market.
The FLEET offering is a software or data service and contains no battery placed on the market; the Batteries Regulation applies to battery-containing hardware, not to the service itself.
FLEET is not a recreational craft or RCD component.
FLEET is not shipborne MED equipment.
The revised PLD covers software; a defective fleet service can cause economic and safety-relevant loss.

FLEET is defined as a B2B service sold to professional operators, so the consumer distance-selling rules (CRD) do not apply to that relationship; B2B terms and business-to-business fairness rules apply instead.
FLEET does not transmit or receive radio signals; connectivity is provided by operators and devices.
FLEET processes vessel and personnel data as processor/controller; GDPR, LOPDGDD and Article 28 DPA obligations apply, likely with a DPIA.
